title: Rome distorts Reformed denial of inherent formal justification
source_text: XXV. Porro haec sententiae Orthodoxae explicatio probe animadvertenda est contra Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, qui Reformatorum hac in parte doctrinam aut non intelligunt, aut malitiose detorquent. Quum enim audiunt Scholae Reformatae Doctores passim dicentes, nos coram Deo justificari, & justos constitui per justitiam Christi quae nobis imputatur, non vero per ullam nobis inhaerentem justitiam, inde colligunt nos non agnoscere justitiam ullam quae fidelibus insit, & cujus ratione vere apud Deum justi & sancti censeantur, nosque traducunt quasi doceremus fideles semper in se impios, immundos, & injustos manere: Christi vero justitiam ad hoc solum illis imputari ut peccata eorum tegantur, non tollantur. Ac proinde, quum fideles justi & sancti in Scriptura vocantur, denominationem istam non sumi ab aliqua forma, sive justitia quae ipsis inhaereat, sed a sola justitia Christi, quae cum extra eos sit, illos tamen denominet, quoniam illis a Deo imputatur.
pass_a_gloss: Further, this explanation of the Orthodox judgment must be carefully noted against the doctors of the Roman Church, who either do not understand the Reformers’ doctrine on this point or maliciously twist it. For when they hear the Reformed-school doctors saying everywhere that we are justified before God and constituted just by Christ’s righteousness which is imputed to us, not by any righteousness inhering in us, they thence gather that we acknowledge no righteousness that is in the faithful and by reason of which they are truly reckoned just and holy before God, and they traduce us as if we taught that the faithful always remain in themselves impious, unclean, and unjust: and that Christ’s righteousness is imputed to them only so that their sins are covered, not taken away. And therefore, when the faithful are called just and holy in Scripture, that denomination is not taken from any form or righteousness inhering in them, but from Christ’s righteousness alone, which, though outside them, nevertheless denominates them because it is imputed to them by God.
pass_b_english: Rome hears “justified by imputed, not inherent” and charges denial of all inward holiness.
Calumny: believers stay impure within; imputation only covers, never removes, sin.

lemmas.gloss: sins are covered, not taken away
